text.p: Members of the United Steelworkers of America employed by the Bridgestone/Firestone Corp voted by a 3-1 margin Thursday to approve a new contract, ending a labor dispute that began in 1994, the union said.

The contract covers workers at the Bridgestone Corp subsidiary's plants in Akron, Ohio; Noblesville, Ind.; Des Moines, Iowa; Decatur, Ill.; Oklahoma City, Okla.; and Russellville, Ark. It was effective upon ratification and expires April 23, 2000, the union said Friday.
It noted workers at the company's LaVergne, Tenn., plant will vote Dec. 18 on a separate agreement.

The ratification brings to an end a dispute that began July 12, 1994, when workers struck at all plants except Russellville. Although the strike ended on May 22, 1995, an agreement proved elusive until the two parties met in Chicago last month when 72 hours of non-stop bargaining led to a tentative agreement on November 4.

Among other things, the union said, the new contract calls for all union members who have not yet been recalled to be returned to their jobs, and it provides amnesty to more than 40 workers who were discharged for alleged strike-related misconduct.

The contract also includes wage increases; a $750 bonus for all employees; $16 million in supplemental bonuses for returned strikers; a $4 increase in the monthly pension multiplier; restoration of holidays to a total of 11; health program improvements; and complete elimination of health insurance premiums, the steelworkers said.
